- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 7–14 days.  
- If sentiment drops sharply (e.g., from 0.8 to -0.2), model may overreact to recent spikes; cap forecast increase after 3–5 days of high sentiment.  
- If true price drops >5% from recent peak, model often overshoots; apply mean reversion correction: subtract 0.5–1.5x the drop from forecast.  
- If sentiment is flat or negative, model tends to lag; add 0.5–1.0x the recent average drop to forecast for next 3–5 days.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true price deviates >10% from 14-day moving average, adjust forecast to align with recent trend, not long-term slope.
